stray-kids.en:
Stray Kids are an eight-member boy group under JYP Entertainment, formed through the 2017 survival program of the same name and debuting on 25 March 2018. Unlike many idol groups that receive songs fully written by external producers, Stray Kids built their identity as a self-producing unit: Bang Chan, Changbin and Han form the production crew 3RACHA, and the group co-writes and co-produces the majority of their discography. Members are Bang Chan (leader, Australia-raised), Lee Know, Changbin, Hyunjin, Han, Felix (Australia-raised), Seungmin and I.N. Their official fandom name is STAY.

Origins and identity. The group nearly lost members during their pre-debut show, then reclaimed a full eight-person line-up - a story STAY still treat as founding mythology. Conceptually they lean into "kids who stray from the ordinary": misfit energy, loud live vocals, dual-unit stages (e.g. vocal vs rap lines), and dense, genre-blending title tracks. Landmark eras include God's Menu (the "cooking" performance era that went viral for choreography), MANIAC / ODDINARY, MAXIDENT, 5-STAR (S-Class), ROCK-STAR (LALALALA), ATE (Chk Chk Boom) and special album HOP. They have sold out dome and stadium-scale tours worldwide and rank among the strongest 4th-generation global acts by touring and physical album metrics.

Where they are from. Bang Chan and Felix spent formative years in Sydney, Australia, and often switch between Korean and English on lives. Other members are Korean-born and trained in Seoul's JYP system. The bilingual presence shapes their global variety content, English ment segments and international press comfort.

Food, drinks and daily life (public variety trivia). Felix is famous among fans for loving spicy food and chicken, and for a deep voice that contrasts with a soft off-stage personality; he has also talked about baking and desserts on lives. Bang Chan is often seen with coffee during late-night producing streams. Changbin jokes about protein-heavy meals around training. Han has mentioned comfort snacks during long studio nights. Seungmin and I.N appear frequently in food-related variety segments - Korean BBQ, ramen late nights, and convenience-store runs after schedules are a recurring STAY meme. On tour, staff-managed diets tighten for vocal health; off-tour, members share more casual cafe drinks (Americanos, fruitades) on Weverse and Instagram stories. These details come from publicly broadcast variety shows, lives and fan-translated interviews - not private medical or confidential information.

Music and craft. Expect aggressive brass and trap-influenced title tracks, melodic b-sides, SKZ-Player / SKZ-Record free releases, and annual fanmeeting lore. Official Light Stick Ver.2 and SKZOO character merch define the concert sea of light. Charting is driven by multi-version album drops, pre-order events and STAY streaming parties.

How to follow. Official hub: straykids.jype.com, Weverse community, Spotify / Apple Music / YouTube Music artist pages, and the @StrayKids YouTube channel for MVs and SKZ CODE variety. For concerts, use Ticketmaster region sites, Interpark Global for Korea, and always verify against JYP notices. BiasDrop lists tour dates as a fan guide only - confirm seat maps and ages on official sellers before paying.

Super-fan checklist. Collect photocards by album version, sleeve everything, learn fanchants for title tracks, and respect venue light-stick rules. Support official merch via Weverse Shop or licensed retailers rather than unverified resellers when possible.

Career milestones and cultural impact. Across comebacks, the group has contributed to the global normalization of Korean-language pop on Western charts, festival bills and stadium calendars. Physical album culture - multiple photobook versions, posters, stickers and random photocards - turned each release into a collecting event. Fan projects (charity donations, birthday ads, streaming parties) sit beside official promotions. Critics sometimes debate over-saturation of idol content; fans answer with sustained touring demand and multi-year loyalty metrics that few entertainment industries can match.

Training, performance and craft. Idol training typically includes vocal coaching, dance precision, media etiquette, language study and extreme schedule discipline. What audiences see on music-show stages is the tip of a pyramid of rehearsals, formations drilled to the count, and live-vocal risk under choreography. Self-producing members blur the line between idol and auteur: beat-making in hotel rooms, lyric notes on phones, late Weverse updates after studio sessions. Choreographers and performance directors co-author the visual language - formations that read on stadium LED, points for fancams, and breaks designed for light-stick waves.

Fandom infrastructure. Modern fandoms run on Weverse communities, Twitter/X trending, TikTok challenges, Discord servers and local city meetups. Streaming guides explain playlist hygiene, smart-shuffle pitfalls and the difference between algorithmic passive plays and intentional charting. Photocard trading has its own etiquette: clear photos, tracked shipping, group proofs, and block lists for scammers. Concert queues reward early information: venue bag policies, medical stations, official merch trucks, and accessibility seating.

Food, drink and lifestyle (public entertainment context only). Variety programs, lives and travel shows surface snack preferences, regional dishes and cafe habits. These are performance-adjacent personas shaped by cameras, sponsorships and editing - not comprehensive private diets. On tour, nutrition staff often prioritize vocal cord health, hydration, anti-inflammatory meals and sleep. Off-tour, members may share more casual ramen, BBQ, desserts or hometown comfort food. Fans should avoid body-shaming commentary; celebrating recipes and cultural food moments is different from policing idols' bodies.

How BiasDrop presents this artist. Our encyclopedia page aggregates publicly known career facts, streaming links (Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music), official community hubs and a fan-guide concert radar. Images on cards may use official music-video thumbnails from YouTube for recognition - always click through to official channels. Bios are written for super-fan orientation in Bulgarian and English; they are not authorized biographies. For interviews and exclusive statements, rely on agency press releases and verified Weverse posts.

Further listening path. Start with the title-track MVs on the official YouTube channel, then explore b-sides that show vocal color and rap writing. Sample a full album version pack if you collect; otherwise prioritize one standard version plus digital streaming. Learn one fanchant before a concert. Follow tour news on Ticketmaster regional sites, Songkick/Bandsintown alerts, and the group's official site. Support with legal streams and official merch so the industry metrics that fund the next world tour stay healthy.


Members and roles in the public eye. Leaders coordinate ment energy and crisis communication; main dancers anchor formations; main vocals carry live bridges; rappers shape title-track attitude. Cross-line friendships visible on variety shows humanize the machine of promotion weeks. International members often become bridges for world tours - English, Japanese or Chinese ments that turn arenas into multi-lingual rooms. Unit songs allow sub-fandoms to bloom without breaking group identity.

Touring logistics for fans. International tickets may require local account registration, queue-it waiting rooms, face-value limits and dynamic pricing. Passport names must match IDs at door. Secondary markets inflate prices and risk invalid barcodes - prefer official resale tools when available. Travel: book refundable lodging until seats are secured; check transit strikes; download offline maps around the venue. Ear protection for loud EDM-leaning title tracks is smart, not uncool. After-parties are unofficial - stay safe in groups.

Collecting culture depth. Photocards range from common album pulls to limited pre-order benefits, broadcast benefits and lucky draws. Grading culture (from other hobbies) is seeping in; most K-pop collectors still prefer personal binders over sealed speculation. Display with UV protection if near windows. Digitize your collection inventory to avoid double-buys. Seasonal greetings packages blend stationery, desk kits and exclusive PCs - budget them as holiday gifts to yourself.

Ethics and longevity. Do not stalk dorms, airports or private family events. Do not spread deepfakes or non-consensual photos. Support mental-health messaging when idols speak about rest. Celebrate comebacks without attacking other fandoms. The healthiest super fans outlast single eras because they attach to craft and community, not only chart wars.
